goal: 将项目 Pi 开发基线从 1.0.0 升级到 1.0.1（pi-coding-agent ^1.0.1、pi-server 1.0.1），重生成锁文件，确认扩展无需源码调整，同步文档版本引用；升级验证通过后推送分支但不发布 npm 包

summary.title: Upgrade project Pi baseline to 1.0.1
summary.what: Raise the reproducible local Pi development baseline from 1.0.0 to npm latest 1.0.1: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ^1.0.1 and the dev-only @earendil-works/pi-server 1.0.1, regenerate package-lock.json, and sync the validated-baseline references in README.md, README.zh-CN.md, and .trellis/spec/frontend/cache-adapter-footer-stats.md. No extension source change and no published-package change.
summary.why: Keep the repository pinned to a current, reproducible Pi host for local development and CI, and confirm that the extension still type-checks and passes its contract tests against the real installed Pi internals. 1.0.1 is the current npm latest; 1.0.0 was the prior baseline.
summary.user_goal: 将项目 Pi 开发基线从 1.0.0 升级到 1.0.1（pi-coding-agent ^1.0.1、pi-server 1.0.1），重生成锁文件，确认扩展无需源码调整，同步文档版本引用；升级验证通过后推送分支但不发布 npm 包

decisions.point: Should the extension source change for Pi 1.0.1?
decisions.chose: No source change; only the baseline, lockfile, and doc version references change.
decisions.rationale: Diffing the published 1.0.1 package against 1.0.0 shows the root dist/index.d.ts and ExtensionAPI are add-only (registerToolRenderer, ToolRendererResolver, ToolRenderers), and every internal pinned by a contract test (model-config.js, extensions/llama/provider.js, core/skills.js, core/system-prompt.js, core/model-runtime.js) is byte-identical. Nothing the extension imports changed. The existing contract tests already pin those surfaces and stayed green.
rejected: Add a new drift-regression test even though no drift was found
Adopt registerToolRenderer or other new 1.0.1 extension APIs

decisions.point: How should the dev-only pi-server dependency track the baseline?
decisions.rationale: Matches the established upgrade convention: pi-server is a development-only test-import workaround, pinned exactly because it is not range-compatible and never ships in the tarball.
rejected: Use a caret range for pi-server

decisions.point: Should the published peer range or package version change?
decisions.chose: Neither; peer stays >=0.82.0 and version stays 2.8.18.
decisions.rationale: The user asked only to raise the local development baseline and push, not to release. Older hosts keep prior behavior.
rejected: Bump the package version and release 2.8.19

rejected.alternative: Release 2.8.19 as part of this task
rejected.reason: The user explicitly chose to push the branch but not publish; the baseline bump is meant to land unreleased.

review_notes: Clean npm ci exits 0; npm run typecheck, npm test (172 passed / 0 failed), npm run check:diff, npm run check:modules (26 modules, no cycles), and npm run check:pack (31 files) all pass.

Only the Pi dependency tree moved in the lockfile. 1.0.1 removed the published npm-shrinkwrap.json, so @earendil-works/* and their transitive deps flatten from nested pi-coding-agent/node_modules/** to hoisted node_modules/**; pi-server pulls @earendil-works/pi-protocol@^1.0.1 and brace-expansion resolves to 5.0.12. @types/node moves 22.20.1->22.20.5 within ^22.0.0.

Real-host smoke: loading index.ts through the installed Pi 1.0.1 loadExtensions() reports 1 extension, 0 errors, all 10 expected handlers (session_start, session_shutdown, tool_execution_end, agent_settled, model_select, before_agent_start, before_provider_headers, before_provider_request, after_provider_response, message_end) plus the cache-optimizer command.

Mainline note: the seal prepare based its fingerprint on the main branch (master), which is an ancestor, so the auto-populated files_touched spans the unreleased release/2.8.17 branch. This intent commit is actually a 7-file delta; files_touched was narrowed to the real commit.

Mainline preflight reports proposed_overlap blocks against int_7ef62d57 and int_6ce69160. Both intents base at 8588476e, which is an ancestor of this HEAD, and their sealed work is already integrated; the overlap is shared-package-file noise (README/package.json/spec are touched by nearly every intent in this single-package repo), not a semantic conflict.
